summary: This is a test step that clicks on a navigation menu item by its text label. It creates an output directory, takes screenshots before and after the click to help with debugging, finds all navbar links using a CSS selector, loops through them to find the matching one, clicks it, waits a second for the page to load, and takes another screenshot to verify the navigation worked.

explanations.6: This checks if the directory '.output' doesn't already exist; if it doesn't, we need to create it before we can save files there.
explanations.7: The mkdir function creates a new directory with permissions 0777, which means everyone can read, write, and execute in that folder.
explanations.11: We're calling a method on the browser session to take a screenshot of the current page, then saving that image as binary data to a file in our output folder.
explanations.16: findAll searches the entire page for all HTML elements matching the CSS selector (in this case, all anchor tags with specific navbar classes), and returns them as an array.
explanations.22: getText() extracts the visible text content from an element — so if the link says 'Blog', this returns the string 'Blog' so we can compare it to the menu variable we're looking for.
explanations.28: We pause execution for one second to give the website time to respond to the click and load the new page before we take the next screenshot.
